Setting and framing: Continue the exact Scene 01 source view, with the same Sol, bough, clearing and lighting. Generate at the original medium-wide framing. The tighter response view is an editing-only digital push; endpoint assets remain uncropped.
Lighting: Keep Scene 01's soft overcast upper-left light and faint warmth immediately around the existing bough fire.
Camera in generation: Generation: stable camera, no zoom or crop change.
Editing: After the brief matching opening, apply one controlled digital push from 100% to 120%, anchored at x=50%, y=56%, then hold. Keep the full flame tip, feet and bough visible; do not ask generation to duplicate this move. Keep the digital move smooth over stepped source footage; enforce source-state pairs first and check crops throughout the full move.
First frame: Reuse Scene 01's approved last image unchanged: Sol holds one short arm toward the bough, his other arm lowered, feet planted and face directed toward the wood.

Silent gaze-ready lead-in: Sol looks UP to Arthur before his first word. Do not start Arthur's audio until that gaze is established. Planned lead-in about0.3s; final cue follows actual recordings.

Narrator: “We don't know. Natural fires existed long before people.”

Action: Begin in the exact reused Scene 01 ending pose. Immediately lift the original navy eye pair toward the fixed Narrator point just above camera; establish the upward glance in the short opening transition, before the Narrator's first word. Lower the presenting arm once along a short direct path to its flank, with constant stubby length and attachment. Keep the gaze UP for the entire listening section and maintain gentle low-amplitude connected body/tip/lobe idle while Arthur speaks. The arms remain quiet after lowering, feet supported, and normal oval design/spacing intact around an optional brief natural blink. Do not turn attention back to the fire during Arthur's turn.
